'''Hans Lischka''' (born July 26, 1943) is an Austrian [[Theoretical chemistry|computational theoretical chemist]] specialized on development and application of [[Multireference configuration interaction|multireference methods]] for the study of [[Excited state|molecular excited states]].<ref name="lischka2018">{{cite journal |last1=Lischka |first1=Hans |last2=Nachtigallová |first2=Dana |last3=Aquino |first3=Adélia J. A. |last4=Szalay |first4=Péter G. |last5=Plasser |first5=Felix |last6=Machado |first6=Francisco B. C. |last7=Barbatti |first7=Mario |author-link7=Mario Barbatti |title=Multireference Approaches for Excited States of Molecules |journal=Chemical Reviews |date=24 July 2018 |volume=118 |issue=15 |pages=7293–7361 |doi=10.1021/acs.chemrev.8b00244 |pmid=30040389|s2cid=206542530 |url=https://hal-amu.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-01965456/file/p128_Lischka_mr-methods_ChemRev_2018-preprint.pdf }}</ref> He is the main developer of the software package [[Columbus (software)|Columbus]]<ref name="lischka2011">{{cite journal |last1=Lischka |first1=Hans |last2=Müller |first2=Thomas |last3=Szalay |first3=Péter G. |last4=Shavitt |first4=Isaiah |last5=Pitzer |first5=Russell M. |last6=Shepard |first6=Ron |title=Columbus-a program system for advanced multireference theory calculations |journal=Wiley Interdisciplinary Reviews: Computational Molecular Science |date=March 2011 |volume=1 |issue=2 |pages=191–199 |doi=10.1002/wcms.25|s2cid=95898474 }}</ref> for ab initio [[Multireference configuration interaction|multireference calculations]] and co-developer of the [[Newton-X|Newton-X program]].

== Biography, education and career==

Hans Lischka was born in Vienna, in 1943, and studied chemistry at the [[University of Vienna]], where he earned a Ph.D. in 1969, being supervised by Gerhard Derflinger. He was a postdoc with [[Werner Kutzelnigg]] at the [[Karlsruhe Institute of Technology|University of Karlsruhe]] in 1972-1973 and got his [[habilitation]] in theoretical chemistry in 1976.<ref name="barbatti2008">{{cite journal |last1=Barbatti |first1=Mario |author-link1=Mario Barbatti |last2=Köppel |first2=Horst |last3=Shepard |first3=Ron |last4=Szalay |first4=Péter G. |title=Electron correlation and molecular dynamics for excited states and photochemistry |journal=Chemical Physics |date=June 2008 |volume=349 |issue=1–3 |pages=vii–viii |doi=10.1016/j.chemphys.2008.05.017 |bibcode=2008CP....349D...7B}}</ref>

In 1980, he was a visiting professor with [[Isaiah Shavitt]] at the [[Ohio State University]], where he started the development of a set of codes for multireference calculations in collaboration with Ron Shepard, Frank Brown, and [[Russell M. Pitzer]]. This set of programs later became the [[Columbus program|Columbus]] system.<ref name="shepard1988">{{cite journal |last1=Shepard |first1=Ron |last2=Shavitt |first2=Isaiah |last3=Pitzer |first3=Russell M. |last4=Comeau |first4=Donald C. |last5=Pepper |first5=Melanie |last6=Lischka |first6=Hans |last7=Szalay |first7=Peter G. |last8=Ahlrichs |first8=Reinhart |last9=Brown |first9=Franklin B. |last10=Zhao |first10=Jian-Guo |title=A progress report on the status of the COLUMBUSMRCI program system |journal=International Journal of Quantum Chemistry |date=12 March 1988 |volume=34 |issue=S22 |pages=149–165 |doi=10.1002/qua.560340819}}</ref> Hans Lischka became a professor of theoretical chemistry at the University of Vienna also in 1980.<ref name="barbatti2008" />

Between 2011 and 2015, Hans Lischka was a research professor at [[Texas Tech University]] in [[Lubbock, Texas]]. In 2015, he took a position as professor at the [[Tianjin University|School of Pharmaceutical Sciences, Tianjin University]] in [[Tianjin|Tianjin, China]].

In addition to his academic work, Lischka has served as the director of the Institute for Theoretical Chemistry and Radiation Chemistry of the University of Vienna (1992–1996), head of the section Vienna, Lower Austria and Burgenland of the Austrian Chemical Society (1993–1995) and vice director of the Institute for Theoretical Chemistry and Structural Biology (2000–2004).{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}

== Honors and awards ==

* 1980 [[Sandoz]] Prize for Chemistry
* 2008 Festschrift in ''[[Chemical Physics (journal)|Chemical Physics]]''.<ref>{{cite web |title=ScienceDirect |url=https://www.sciencedirect.com/journal/chemical-physics/vol/349/issue/1 |website=www.sciencedirect.com}}</ref>
* 2008 International Symposium on “Electron Correlation and Molecular Dynamics for Excited States and Photochemistry”, International Symposium in honor of Hans Lischka's 65th birthday, July 4, 2008{{citation needed|date=May 2025}}

== Scientific contributions, interests and achievements ==

Lischka is responsible for the development and implementation of highly parallelized MRCI, with analytical energy gradients<ref name="lischka2002">{{cite journal |last1=LISCHKA |first1=H. |last2=DALLOS |first2=M. |last3=SHEPARD |first3=R. |title=Analytic MRCI gradient for excited states: formalism and application to the n-π∗ valence- and n-(3s,3p) Rydberg states of formaldehyde |journal=Molecular Physics |date=10 June 2002 |volume=100 |issue=11 |pages=1647–1658 |doi=10.1080/00268970210155121|bibcode=2002MolPh.100.1647L |s2cid=97307361 }}</ref> and analytical nonadiabatic couplings.<ref name="lischka2004">{{cite journal |last1=Lischka |first1=Hans |last2=Dallos |first2=Michal |last3=Szalay |first3=Péter G. |last4=Yarkony |first4=David R. |last5=Shepard |first5=Ron |title=Analytic evaluation of nonadiabatic coupling terms at the MR-CI level. I. Formalism |journal=The Journal of Chemical Physics |date=22 April 2004 |volume=120 |issue=16 |pages=7322–7329 |doi=10.1063/1.1668615|pmid=15267642 |bibcode=2004JChPh.120.7322L |s2cid=21157929 }}</ref> These methods later became the heart of the [[Newton-X]] program.<ref name="barbatti2007">{{cite journal |last1=Barbatti |first1=Mario |author-link1=Mario Barbatti |last2=Granucci |first2=Giovanni |last3=Persico |first3=Maurizio |last4=Ruckenbauer |first4=Matthias |last5=Vazdar |first5=Mario |last6=Eckert-Maksić |first6=Mirjana |last7=Lischka |first7=Hans |title=The on-the-fly surface-hopping program system Newton-X: Application to ab initio simulation of the nonadiabatic photodynamics of benchmark systems |journal=Journal of Photochemistry and Photobiology A: Chemistry |date=August 2007 |volume=190 |issue=2–3 |pages=228–240 |doi=10.1016/j.jphotochem.2006.12.008 |bibcode=2007JPPA..190..228B }}</ref> In 2010, Lischka's group published the first ab initio mapping of the deactivation mechanism of UV-excited canonical nucleobases.<ref name="barbatti2010">{{cite journal |last1=Barbatti |first1=M. |author-link1=Mario Barbatti |last2=Aquino |first2=A. J. A. |last3=Szymczak |first3=J. J. |last4=Nachtigallova |first4=D. |last5=Hobza |first5=P. |last6=Lischka |first6=H. |title=Relaxation mechanisms of UV-photoexcited DNA and RNA nucleobases |journal=Proceedings of the National Academy of Sciences |date=29 November 2010 |volume=107 |issue=50 |pages=21453–21458 |doi=10.1073/pnas.1014982107|pmid=21115845 |bibcode=2010PNAS..10721453B |pmc=3003128 |doi-access=free }}</ref>

His current research interests include method developments in multireference theory<ref name="das2017">{{cite journal |last1=Das |first1=Anita |last2=Müller |first2=Thomas |last3=Plasser |first3=Felix |last4=Krisiloff |first4=David B. |last5=Carter |first5=Emily A. |last6=Lischka |first6=Hans |title=Local Electron Correlation Treatment in Extended Multireference Calculations: Effect of Acceptor–Donor Substituents on the Biradical Character of the Polycyclic Aromatic Hydrocarbon Heptazethrene |journal=Journal of Chemical Theory and Computation |date=2 May 2017 |volume=13 |issue=6 |pages=2612–2622 |doi=10.1021/acs.jctc.7b00156 |pmid=28441477 |bibcode=2017JCTC...13.2612D |s2cid=4232789 |url=https://dspace.lboro.ac.uk/2134/32230}}</ref> and computational photodynamics.<ref name="cardozo2019">{{cite journal |last1=Cardozo |first1=Thiago Messias |last2=Galliez |first2=Andre Pessoa |last3=Borges |first3=Itamar |last4=Plasser |first4=Felix |last5=Aquino |first5=Adelia J. A. |last6=Barbatti |first6=Mario |author-link6=Mario Barbatti |last7=Lischka |first7=Hans |title=Dynamics of benzene excimer formation from the parallel-displaced dimer |journal=Physical Chemistry Chemical Physics |volume=21 |issue=26 |pages=13916–13924 |date=2019 |doi=10.1039/c8cp06354k|pmid=30570626 |bibcode=2019PCCP...2113916C |s2cid=58542427 |url=https://hal-amu.archives-ouvertes.fr/hal-01965447/document }}</ref> His work is also concerned with applications of [[computational chemistry]] to graphene defects,<ref name="plasser2013">{{cite journal |last1=Plasser |first1=Felix |last2=Pašalić |first2=Hasan |last3=Gerzabek |first3=Martin H. |last4=Libisch |first4=Florian |last5=Reiter |first5=Rafael |last6=Burgdörfer |first6=Joachim |last7=Müller |first7=Thomas |last8=Shepard |first8=Ron |last9=Lischka |first9=Hans |title=The Multiradical Character of One- and Two-Dimensional Graphene Nanoribbons |journal=Angewandte Chemie International Edition |date=25 February 2013 |volume=52 |issue=9 |pages=2581–2584 |doi=10.1002/anie.201207671 |pmid=23355507 |pmc=3648980 }}</ref> polyradicloid systems,<ref name="das2016">{{cite journal |last1=Das |first1=Anita |last2=Müller |first2=Thomas |last3=Plasser |first3=Felix |last4=Lischka |first4=Hans |title=Polyradical Character of Triangular Non-Kekulé Structures, Zethrenes, -Quinodimethane-Linked Bisphenalenyl, and the Clar Goblet in Comparison: An Extended Multireference Study |journal=The Journal of Physical Chemistry A |date=25 February 2016 |volume=120 |issue=9 |pages=1625–1636 |doi=10.1021/acs.jpca.5b12393 |pmid=26859789 |pmc=4789636 |bibcode=2016JPCA..120.1625D}}</ref> organic photovoltaics,<ref name="borges2013">{{cite journal |last1=Borges |first1=Itamar |last2=Aquino |first2=Adélia J. A. |last3=Köhn |first3=Andreas |last4=Nieman |first4=Reed |last5=Hase |first5=William L. |last6=Chen |first6=Lin X. |last7=Lischka |first7=Hans |title=Modeling of Excitonic and Charge-Transfer States in Organic Semiconductors: The PTB1/PCBM Low Band Gap System |journal=Journal of the American Chemical Society |date=25 November 2013 |volume=135 |issue=49 |pages=18252–18255 |doi=10.1021/ja4081925 |pmid=24215627}}</ref> interacting nucleobases,<ref name="plasser2013a">{{cite journal |last1=Plasser |first1=Felix |last2=Lischka |first2=Hans |title=Electronic excitation and structural relaxation of the adenine dinucleotide in gas phase and solution |journal=Photochemical & Photobiological Sciences |date=2013 |volume=12 |issue=8 |pages=1440–52 |doi=10.1039/c3pp50032b |pmid=23737069|doi-access=free |bibcode=2013PhPhS..12.1440P }}</ref> and non-covalent interactions.<ref name="pasalic2017">{{cite journal |last1=Pašalić |first1=Hasan |last2=Aquino |first2=Adelia J.
